newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-CU profits growth held back by pound.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-CU profits growth held back by pound.

text.p: Strong performances from life and overseas general insurance operations gave a boost to half-year profits at Commercial Union Plc on Wednesday despite a hefty currency hit.
Trading profits rose eight percent to 235 million pounds over the six months as sterling wiped some 40 million pounds off headline numbers.
UK general insurance continued to struggle with profits sinking nearly 50 million pounds to just 22 million pounds over the six months.
CU chief executive John Carter declared himself happy with the overall performance and said the group was well positioned for the future.
The company also admitted it remained on the lookout for further acquisitions in the life sector both in eastern and western Europe.
But it ruled out the possibility of a larger deal.
Rumours of a tie-up between CU and either ABN AMRO or B.A.T's insurance business have dogged the company in recent months.
Carter said he saw no need to make such a move and also discounted following Prudential Corp and Standard Life into banking.
Analysts suggested the absence of a large deal as the likely reason for a decline in the shares which shed three pence to 686-1/2 pence despite profits topping analyst expectations.
Life business and higher profits from overseas general insurance businesses over the first half offset lower general insurance results in the UK where rates remain in the doldrums.

The UK with a 17 percent increase in profits, together with the Netherlands and France led the way on the life side while the fast growing Polish operation which was only set up in 1992 produced a seven million pound profit, up from one million pounds last year.
Life profits rose eight million pounds to 125 million pounds but at constant exchange rates recorded a 24 percent advance.
They have increased 50 percent in the past two years and now account for around half of the group's business.
The French business is expected to move forward strongly after 1998 following the reorganisation of the sales force which is currently underway.
In general insurance a 47 million pound drop in weather claims produced a turnaround in the U.S. performance while France and Australia also performed well.
But the UK continued to be hit by competition.
Subsidence claims rose again, increasing eight million pounds to 23 million pounds.
UK Rates were described as 'bumping along the bottom' with the London market rates down 10 percent from year ago levels.
Rates in France were also said to be becoming more competitive.
But the group said that the restructuring of UK non life businesses announced two months ago is on target to produce the 100 million pounds of savings forecast.

The group raised the dividend by seven percent to 12.25 pence a share. Following changes in the July budget it will be paid in the form of foreign income dividend, which will reduce the impact of irrecoverable advance corporation tax on the group.
Group total premium income rose to 4.27 billion pounds from 4.04 billion pounds at constant exchange rates.
Net asset value per share rose to 573 pence, up from 545 pence at the end of 1996.
